results.title: Daegu mayor acquitted of obstructing martial law vote
results.content: Daegu Mayor Choo Kyung-ho was acquitted Wednesday of charges of obstructing a National Assembly vote to lift former President Yoon Suk Yeol's martial law declaration in late 2024, when he was the floor leader of the then ruling People Power Party (PPP). The Seoul Central District Court delivered the verdict in the case against Choo, who stood trial on charges of playing a key role in Yoon's alleged insurrection. Choo was accused of changing the venue of an emergency party meeting three times on Dec. 3, 2024, after Yoon declared martial law, in an attempt to prevent lawmakers from taking part in a parliamentary vote on ending the emergency decree. Of the 108 PPP lawmakers, 90 were unable to attend the vote to lift the martial law at the time. Special counsel Cho Eun-suk's team had requested a 20-year prison term for Choo. results.title: Seoul Barbecue Festival draws 20,800 visitors, positive reviews
results.content: Seoul's appetite for outdoor dining proved strong as its annual barbecue festival drew 20,800 visitors over two days, with more than nine in 10 attendees saying they were satisfied with the event. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that the 2026 Seoul Barbecue Festival, held Oct. 24-25 at Nanji Camping Ground, recorded an overall satisfaction rating of 92.7 percent, up 6.2 percentage points from last year. The same proportion of respondents said they intended to return next year, while 91.6 percent said they would recommend the festival to others. The festival featured special menus from prominent chefs, outdoor dining experiences and food stalls showcasing Korean barbecue and regional specialties. Its self-service barbecue zone proved particularly popular, allowing visitors to purchase Korean pork and beef from participating suppliers, including the Korea Pork Producers As

results.title: More Koreans say people should marry, but lack of funds remains top barrier
results.content: Kim, a 41-year-old office worker in Seoul, is getting married this month. As he had remained single longer than many of his peers, his parents began to worry that he might never marry. But Kim had never thought of marriage as something he would forgo. “People may be more skeptical about marriage these days, but I’ve never thought I’d stay single,” he said. “I wanted an ordinary life with a spouse and children, and I wanted that sense of stability. To me, an ordinary life is happiness.” With Seoul home prices out of reach, Kim and his partner opted for a jeonse rental, which requires a large upfront deposit. Even then, they barely managed to cover the deposit with help from both sets of parents. “Housing takes up most of what it costs to get married,” Kim said. “We cut back on the dress, the suit and the jewelry to put more toward housing. results.title: 'Bogum Magical' to join other shows in editing out embattled actor Ko
results.content: The production team behind the upcoming second season of tvN’s variety show “Bogum Magical” said Wednesday that it would seek to minimize viewer discomfort over cast Ko Kyung-pyo’s appearance, following his drunk driving crash. “We are bewildered by this unexpected situation and deeply regret it,” the team said Wednesday in a statement. The announcement came as broadcasters and streaming platforms moved to reduce Ko's screen time after a drunk driving incident involving the actor. Debuted in 2010, Ko is known for his roles in the film "Decision to Leave" (2022) and TV series "Reply 1988" (2015). He joined "Bogum Magical" as a new cast in the second series, which is scheduled for release in Korea and on multiple global streaming platforms later this month. results.title: JB Financial, Ant Group team up on AI credit scoring for foreign customers
results.content: JB Financial Group has teamed up with China's Ant Group to improve credit assessment systems using artificial intelligence (AI) technology and expand access to financial services for foreign residents in Korea, the group said Wednesday. The group signed a memorandum of understanding with Ant Digital Technologies (Ant DT), Ant Group's digital technology subsidiary, Tuesday at the latter's office in Singapore. The signing took place on the sidelines of the Singapore Fintech Festival 2026. The ceremony was attended by Park Jong-choon, vice president of JB Financial's AX Future Growth Division, and Leo Li, president of international business at Ant DT. Under the partnership, the two companies will explore ways to upgrade credit assessment models and financial services offered by JB Financial's affiliates, including Jeonbuk Bank, Kwangju Bank and JB Woori Capital. results.title: Garden at Mount Nam gets after-dark glow inspired by Korean tradition
results.content: Seoul is giving Mount Nam, the forested peak in the heart of the capital, a new after-dark glow with firefly-inspired lights, illuminated bamboo groves and seasonal palettes drawn from traditional Korean attire. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that it had completed a nighttime garden project at Namsan Korean Forest Garden, opening the redesigned areas to visitors the same day. The 1,750-square-meter project covers two distinctive sections, Jidangwon and Jukrimwon, and includes a newly created resting area connecting the pine forest with the pond garden. Lighting operates from about 15 minutes after sunset until 11 p.m., with hours subject to seasonal and weather conditions. results.title: Listed firms' profits jump in Q3 on semiconductor boom
results.content: South Korean listed firms posted record earnings during the third quarter of this year, driven by a surge in exports of semiconductors amid global investment for artificial intelligence (AI), data showed Wednesday. The combined operating profit of 717 companies listed on the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) jumped 18.59 percent on-quarter to 195.9 trillion won ($146.6 billion) in the July-September period, according to the data released by the Korea Exchange. Their combined sales rose 7.68 percent on-quarter to 619.3 trillion won, the data showed. However, their combined net profit plunged 35.33 percent on-quarter to 119.4 trillion won, according to the data. Of the total, 391 firms, or 54.53 percent, were in the black. By sector, electric and electronic companies, as well as precision machinery makers, showed solid performances.

results.title: University leaders call for practical AI training, commercialization
results.content: Higher education leaders from Korea, the United States and Vietnam urged campuses on Wednesday to push artificial intelligence (AI) out of the lab and into the marketplace, calling for hands-on training and incentives that reward real-world impact over academic papers. The three panelists spoke during a session on AI commercialization at the Innovation & Impact Summit 2026, hosted by Korea University in Seoul and organized by Times Higher Education, the London-based publisher behind the World University Rankings. Yeom Jae-ho, president of Taejae University and a former president of Korea University, said simply passing knowledge on to students “is not enough in the 21st century.” Taejae University opened in Seoul in 2023 and teaches its classes online in English. results.title: Conglomerate-affiliated firms decline amid portfolio restructuring: FTC
results.content: The antitrust regulator said Wednesday the number of conglomerate-affiliated companies fell slightly from three months earlier, amid industrywide portfolio restructuring efforts. The country's 102 conglomerates held 3,529 affiliates as of Nov. 2, down by five from 3,534 tallied three months earlier, according to the Fair Trade Commission (FTC). Over the period, 65 companies were removed from the list due to mergers, separations and other rearrangements, while 60 were newly added. The FTC said large business groups have conducted portfolio restructuring to seek new business opportunities amid a transition in the overall industrial landscape. Under South Korean law, conglomerates with assets of 5 trillion won ($3.82 billion) or higher are obligated to disclose the status of their businesses, along with details of large-scale internal trade.

results.title: Household credit growth slows in Q3 amid high market rate
results.content: South Korea's household credit growth slowed in the third quarter of the year due to less demand for home purchases and investment-related loans, central bank data showed Wednesday. Outstanding household credit stood at a record 2,030.5 trillion won ($ 1.52 trillion) as of end-September, up 9.8 trillion won from three months earlier, according to the preliminary data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The on-quarter increase marked the slowest since the first quarter of 2025, when the balance rose 2.7 trillion won. Household credit refers to credit purchases and loans extended to households by financial institutions. In detail, household loans stood at 1,896.8 trillion won at the end of September, up 4.7 trillion won from three months earlier, also marking the smallest on-quarter increase since the third quarter of 2025. results.title: Ruling party, gov't unveil revised plan to relocate Army academy to Chungcheong region
results.content: The Army academy will be relocated to the central Chungcheong region, while the Navy and Air Force academies will be kept in place, the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) and the government said Wednesday, revising an earlier plan to merge them into a unified military college. Wednesday's announcement finalizes a revision to the original plan to merge the three academies into a single institution, as the government sought to offer a compromise amid strong pushback from alumni groups, cadets and other stakeholders. The revised plan retains the initial proposal to establish a joint academy at the Jaundae military complex in the central city of Daejeon, about 140 kilometers south of Seoul, but each armed service will keep their existing schools as a regional campus. results.title: Lee, Xi hold 3rd summit on APEC sidelines
results.content: SHENZHEN, China — President Lee Jae Myung held bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Wednesday, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting. It is their third summit since Lee took office in June 2025, with two previous meetings in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province in November 2025 and Beijing in January. The leaders will review progress in bilateral relations and discuss ways to expand mutually beneficial economic cooperation, including trade and investment, presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said in a written briefing issued ahead of the meeting. Attention is also on whether Lee and Xi will discuss possible U.S.-North Korea talks, as U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospect of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and referred to a possible role for Xi. results.title: KDI sharply ups 2027 growth estimate for Korean economy to 3.9% amid AI boom: KDI
results.content: Korea's economy is expected to grow at a faster than earlier expected rate of 3.9 percent in 2027, amid strong global demand driven by the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, a state-run think tank said Wednesday. The 2027 growth estimate by the Korea Development Institute (KDI) is far higher than its earlier projection of 2.2 percent advance in August this year. The KDI also raised its growth estimate for the year by 0.6 percentage point to 3.8 percent over the cited period. The research institute said global demand for semiconductor products continues to remain strong, leading to increased exports and facility investment, which are expected to eventually boost private consumption in 2027. results.title: Can classroom English teaching, AI tutoring coexist?
results.content: With growing interest in international travel and cross-cultural exchange, enthusiasm for learning spoken languages through artificial intelligence (AI) apps has surged. Most adult smartphone users already have one or two language apps installed on their devices. This raises an important question: What if students began practicing spoken English with AI tutors from an early age, when language acquisition is most natural and effective? A few months ago, I wrote about the challenges teachers face in integrating AI into the classroom. This time, I’d like to offer a different perspective: how classroom English instruction and AI tutoring can coexist in a mutually beneficial way. In Korea, many students focus almost exclusively on reading, listening and grammar to boost test scores because grades heavily influence academic success. results.title: From jade rings to flowers: What young Koreans are buying at Namdaemun
results.content: Long known for its wide selection of everyday goods at affordable prices, Namdaemun Market is enjoying renewed attention from younger consumers in Korea, many of whom discover quirky items through viral social media posts. For them, a visit is less about ticking off a shopping list than hunting for distinctive finds that blend nostalgia, practicality and a touch of personal style. From tableware for a home cafe to retro-inspired accessories, here are some tips from young Korean shoppers on what to look for and how to make the most of a treasure hunt at Namdaemun Market. Tableware Tableware is one of the most popular shopping items among young Koreans, including 32-year-old designer Kim Hyun-joo. results.title: Apple, Google, OpenAI face tighter FTC scrutiny over Korean representative rule
results.content: Korea’s antitrust regulator will require major overseas platforms, such as Apple, Google, Alibaba and OpenAI, to designate legal representatives in the country starting in January, tightening their obligations to respond to consumer disputes and regulatory inquiries. The Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said Wednesday it has issued guidelines for designating domestic representatives ahead of the enforcement of a new rule under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, scheduled for Jan. 21. “Overseas businesses that fail to comply with the upcoming law will be subject to immediate FTC investigations,” an FTC official said. “Once the law takes effect and domestic representatives provide a legally effective channel for dealing with overseas businesses, it will greatly help resolve consumer disputes that have been difficult to address.” The measure aims to establish a legally ef

results.title: From pharmacy skin care to home goods: What foreign shoppers are buying from Namdaemun Market
results.content: If there's one thing Victoria Young, a tourist from Canada, is going to do in Korea, it's buy skin care products. But instead of making her way through the usually crowded retail stores, she headed to Namdaemun Market, where she visited a pharmacy she saw online and emerged with 11 items in hand. "A big part of why I came to Korea was skin care, and I saw this pharmacy online, and it had a lot of good reviews — like that's where the locals go — so I figured that'd be a good place to check out," she told The Korea Times outside the pharmacy on Nov. 10. "It's not normal, I guess, back home to have these sorts of pharmacies that are just skin care pharmacies, and to get personalized recommendations from pharmacists who specialize in skin care, so that seems like a really cool experience to have," she added. results.title: HUFS celebrates 60 years of Thai studies with international conference, cultural festival
results.content: Hankuk University of Foreign Studies (HUFS) celebrated the 60th anniversary of its Department of Thai Studies with a series of events, including an international academic conference and a cultural festival, on Nov. 5–6, the university said. Founded in 1966, the department used the anniversary as an opportunity to review its achievements in education and research, explore future directions for Thai studies and discuss ways to expand academic and cultural exchanges between Korea and Thailand. The international conference, titled “Thai Studies Beyond Borders: Transitional Perspectives and Future Directions,” was held on Nov. 5–6 at the library on HUFS’ Seoul campus. results.title: University of Seoul Korean history professor elected to ICOMOS board
results.content: Shin Hee-kweon, a professor in the Department of Korean History at the University of Seoul, has been elected to the board of the International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS), the university said. ICOMOS elected a new board at its 22nd General Assembly, held in Kuching, Malaysia, from Oct. 17-24. Shin was elected alongside experts from 11 other countries, including China, Japan, the Philippines, Nigeria and France. The assembly also elected key officers, including the president, secretary general and vice presidents. Shin is a prominent Korean cultural heritage expert. He currently serves as secretary general of ICOMOS Korea. While working for the Cultural Heritage Administration, now known as the Korea Heritage Service, he served as director of the Changdeok Palace Management Office and head of the Conservation Science Division at the National Palace Museum of Korea. results.title: Taiwanese hit character CAPOO takes over Seoul tourism campaign
results.content: A six-legged cartoon cat-insect hybrid from Taiwan is taking on Seoul's biggest tourist attractions, as the city turns to an overseas character franchise to reach new audiences and draw more visitors from one of its key travel markets. The Seoul Tourism Organization said Tuesday it has partnered with CAPOO, a popular Taiwanese character, for Visit Seoul's first collaboration with an overseas character intellectual property brand. Running from Nov. 23–27, the campaign features three short videos following CAPOO on visits to some of Seoul's best-known attractions, combining Korean traditions, food and unusual travel experiences. In the first video, scheduled for Nov. 19, CAPOO wears traditional Korean hanbok while exploring Gyeongbok Palace and its architecture. results.title: Mom's Touch opens 2nd Japanese franchise, targets 11 stores by year-end
results.content: Mom’s Touch is stepping up its expansion in Japan, opening its second locally franchised restaurant this week as the Korean burger and chicken chain aims to build a network of 11 outlets by the end of the year. The company said Wednesday that Mom’s Touch Itabashi Station will open Friday in Tokyo’s Kita ward, marking its seventh store in Japan and first franchise opening since relocating its Japanese corporate office to Shinjuku in September. Located near the east exit of Itabashi Station on the JR Saikyo Line, the restaurant targets neighborhood residents, office workers and commuters traveling into central Tokyo. Unlike existing company-operated outlets in commercial districts such as Shibuya and Harajuku, the new restaurant is designed to serve everyday dining needs, including casual meals and family outings, through its combination of burgers, chicken and pizza. results.title: Kolmar Korea turns to AI to predict skin safety before cosmetics hit market
results.content: Kolmar Korea is developing artificial intelligence (AI) technology to predict how cosmetic ingredients affect the skin before products are manufactured, in a move aimed at speeding development and strengthening the global competitiveness of its clients. The cosmetics manufacturer said Wednesday that it signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology on Tuesday to jointly develop AI-based technology for predicting skin effects. The agreement was signed by Moon Byung-seok, head of technology research at Kolmar Holdings, and Shin Seok-min, president of the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology. The two organizations will collaborate on research, technical exchanges and performance assessments to develop AI models capable of predicting skin reactions and ingredient absorption. results.title: K-culture gets festive makeover at Korea tourism souvenir fair
results.content: Korea is turning its souvenirs into a festive attraction, bringing 143 companies and institutions together for a three-day fair designed to connect the country's cultural products with visitors and global buyers. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) will host the 2026 Korea Tourism Souvenir Fair from Nov. 20–22 at Dongdaemun Design Plaza in Seoul. Now in its fifth year, the event will be its largest yet, with participation up about 60 percent from last year and 145 exhibition booths showcasing products across design, crafts, fashion, beauty, food and lifestyle categories. This year's theme, “A K-Goods Village Covered in First Snow,” combines traditional Korean colors and patterns with Christmas decorations, with a character called Santa Daegam guiding visitors through the exhibition. results.title: Musinsa Standard brings minimalist fashion to Jeju Island
results.content: Musinsa Standard is bringing its minimalist fashion aesthetic to Jeju Island, opening its first store there as the Korean clothing brand looks to attract both local shoppers and international tourists. The store, located in Donam-dong, Jeju City, will open Nov. 26, marking the brand's 45th domestic location and expanding its retail presence beyond mainland Korea. To mark the opening, Musinsa Standard is introducing 12 limited-edition T-shirt designs developed with local brands Jeju Samdasoo, Bbang Gomi and Slowcoaster. The collection draws on familiar symbols of Jeju, including tangerines, hallabong citrus fruit and dol hareubang stone statues. results.title: SK Chemicals, Seogwipo join hands to recycle waste banners
results.content: SK Chemicals is partnering with Seogwipo City on Jeju Island to establish a circular system that turns discarded banners into new products for reuse in the local community. The company said Wednesday that it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the city to promote the recycling and reuse of waste banners. The ceremony was attended by Seogwipo Mayor Kim Hee-chan and Ko Jeong-seok, head of SK Chemicals' recycling business division, among other officials. The partnership stems from an idea developed during a community problem-solving competition hosted by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in September. Seogwipo joined a consortium that took on a waste banner recycling challenge proposed by SK Chemicals. results.title: Korea ends 2027 with Qatar win but questions remain
results.content: Korea ended the year with a 1-0 win over Qatar on Tuesday as Oh Se-hun headed the only goal of the game. It was a dominant performance and really should have been a more convincing win but the strikers missed chance after chance and the opposing goalkeeper made save after save. Indeed, Qatar was so bad that it took a little sheen off the win. Regardless, it was welcome after losing 3-2 to Saudi Arabia last Friday. This was not just the last game of 2026, but it was the last game of Robert Moreno’s coaching contract. The Spaniard, appointed in September on an interim deal, has now come to the end of that period. He has had six games in charge, with three wins, two losses and one draw. results.title: Trump 'serious' about engaging with N. Korean leader Kim: Rubio
results.content: U.S. President Donald Trump is "serious" about seeking dialogue with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday, amid speculation about a possible meeting between the two during Trump's ongoing Asia trip. Rubio made the remarks to the traveling White House press pool in Manila when asked whether Trump's idea of meeting Kim was a serious proposal or merely a possibility being floated. "It's serious in the sense that I think the president has never viewed meeting and talking to someone as a concession," Rubio said. The secretary added that Trump believes dialogue is necessary to resolve disputes with countries with which the United States has disagreements, reiterating that meeting a foreign leader does not mean endorsing that leader's actions. results.title: Elsevier chairman urges universities to pair optimism with focus, trust
results.content: Youngsuk “YS” Chi, chairman of Dutch academic publisher Elsevier, urged university leaders Wednesday to meet mounting pressures — from tight budgets to artificial intelligence (AI) — with what he called optimism backed by thoughtful action. Chi gave the keynote on the second day of the Innovation & Impact Summit 2026, which Times Higher Education (THE) is holding at Korea University in Seoul from Tuesday to Thursday. The London-based publication is known for its annual World University Rankings. “Many of you are facing tighter budgets. Geopolitical tension is making it harder to work across borders. AI is changing how research is done faster than anyone can write the rules about it,” Chi said. “None of these pressures is new on its own. results.title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics expands substrate, MLCC supply to Nvidia
results.content: Samsung Electro-Mechanics has revised its existing supply agreement with Nvidia to expand supplies of advanced semiconductor package substrates and multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) for the U.S. chipmaker's artificial intelligence (AI) computing platforms, the Korean company said Wednesday. The two sides announced their strategic partnership last month, under which Samsung Electro-Mechanics agreed to supply advanced package substrates for Nvidia's computing and high-speed networking products. Although the companies did not disclose specific financial details this time as well, the expanded partnership includes increased supplies of advanced package substrates for Nvidia's next-generation graphics processing units, additional financial support from Nvidia for Samsung Electro-Mechanics' production facilities in Korea and the inclusion of MLCCs in the supply agreement. results.title: PM asks for people's understanding over alert messages to be sent during college entrance exam
results.content: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook asked for people's understanding Wednesday in connection with disaster alert messages that the government plans to send as part of efforts to prevent cheating during the nationwide college entrance exam this week. Alert messages for the highest level of disasters, which are designed to reach all mobile phones and sound a loud alarm even when the phone is muted, will be sent to detect any hidden mobile phones that can be used to cheat with artificial intelligence (AI) during the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday. "We recognize that receiving these messages may cause some inconvenience," Han said during a meeting with the ruling Democratic Party of Korea and the presidential office Cheong Wa Dae.
